title: Canonical map from chart germs to prime localized fractions
statement: Let $S$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring with grading $\mathcal A$, and $M$ a $\mathbb Z$-graded $S$-module with a grading $\mathcal M$ compatible with scalar multiplication. Set $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Index charts by pairs $f=(a,d)$ with $d>0$ and $a\in S_d$, put $D_f=D_+(a)$, $R_f=S_{(a)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $Z_f$ be submodules of $M_a$ whose carriers are precisely the equal-degree fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose additive maps $\rho_{f,g}:Z_f\to Z_g$ and ring maps $\rho^S_{f,g}:R_f\to R_g$ are given for every $D_g\subseteq D_f$. Suppose each inclusion admits a homogeneous relation $g^e=bf$ with $e>0$, each $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$, and for every such relation it sends $y/f^m$ to $b^my/g^{em}$. Assume identities, composition and bijectivity when chart opens coincide. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with additive chart identifications $\alpha_f:F(D_f)\cong Z_f$ respecting scalars via awayToSection and restrictions via $\rho$. Suppose submodules $Z_p$ of the ordinary prime localizations are given with carriers the equal-degree fractions. There exist additive maps $F_x\to Z_p$, semilinear over stalkIso, sending the germ of every chart fraction $y/f^m$ to the unchanged fraction in the prime localization. Neither injectivity nor surjectivity is asserted; internality of the module grading is not assumed.

proof.text: For x in D(f), powers of f lie in the prime complement. Use LocalizedModule.liftOfLE to map the ordinary chart localization to the prime localization. Its fraction formula preserves numerator and denominator, so hZ and hZp restrict it to an additive map c from Z_f to Z_p. This is an explicit map, with its membership and additive laws proved.

For D(g) contained in D(f), write any q in Z_f as y/f^m using ordinary localization induction and the powers-submonoid witness. Extract g^e=a*f and the rho fraction formula from hlaws. After applying c on both sides, LocalizedModule.mk_eq reduces compatibility to f^m acting on a^m*y equals g^(e*m) acting on y; this follows from the power relation and mul_smul.

Use standardOpenProperties for the positive homogeneous standard-open basis. Given compatible additive maps on an indexed basis, choose a basic germ representative of each stalk element. The basis germ-comparison lemma gives a smaller basic neighbourhood on which any two representatives agree, proving independence. For addition, restrict two representatives to a basic neighbourhood inside their intersection and apply the chart map additivity. Apply this construction to c composed with alpha; hchart gives compatibility. This constructs tau with its chart germ formula.

Represent a scalar stalk element and a module stalk element by sections and restrict both to a common positive standard open. The isomorphism basicOpenIsoAway writes the scalar as awayToSection(a). Use germ_smul and hchart to reduce semilinearity to the scalar compatibility of the localization map. Prove this compatibility on homogeneous scalar fractions and ordinary module fractions using mk_smul_mk and liftOfLE_mk. The equality awayToSection_germ followed by stalkIso identifies the scalar germ with mapId(a). Finally the tau chart formula and liftOfLE_mk give the displayed fraction formula, identifying denominators by subtype extensionality.

lean.statement:
theorem gradedModuleStalkMap
    (𝓜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M)
    (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : S) (y : M),
      a ∈ 𝒜 n → y ∈ 𝓜 z → a • y ∈ 𝓜 (n + z))
    (Z : ∀ f : Fidx, Submodule R[f] N[f])
    (hZ : (∀ f : Fidx, (Z f : Set N[f]) = degreeZeroFractions
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set S)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 n : Set M))
        (Submonoid.powers f.val.1)))
    (rhoS : ∀ (f g : Fidx), D[g] ≤ D[f] → R[f] →+* R[g])
    (rho : ∀ (f g : Fidx), D[g] ≤ D[f] → Z f →+ Z g)
    (hlaws : (∀ (f g : Fidx) (i : D[g] ≤ D[f]),
        (∃ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e ∧ a ∈ 𝒜 k ∧ g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1) ∧
        (∀ (r : R[f]) (q : Z f), rho f g i (r • q) = rhoS f g i r • rho f g i q) ∧
        (∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : S), 0 < e → a ∈ 𝒜 k → g.val.1 ^ e = a * f.val.1 →
          ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : M) (q : Z f),
            (q : N[f]) = mk y (⟨f.val.1 ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1) →
            (rho f g i q : N[g]) = mk (a ^ m • y)
              (⟨g.val.1 ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g.val.1))) ∧
      (∀ (f : Fidx) (i : D[f] ≤ D[f]) (q : Z f), rho f f i q = q) ∧
      (∀ (f g h : Fidx) (i : D[g] ≤ D[f]) (j : D[h] ≤ D[g]) (q : Z f),
        rho g h j (rho f g i q) = rho f h (j.trans i) q) ∧
      (∀ (f g : Fidx) (i : D[g] ≤ D[f]), D[f] = D[g] →
        Function.Bijective (rho f g i)))
    (F : ModX) (alpha : ∀ f : Fidx, F.val.obj (op D[f]) ≃+ Z f)
    (hchart : (∀ (f : Fidx) (r : R[f]) (s : F.val.obj (op D[f])),
        alpha f ((awayToSection 𝒜 f.val.1 r) • s) = r • alpha f s) ∧
      (∀ (f g : Fidx) (i : D[g] ≤ D[f]) (s : F.val.obj (op D[f])),
        alpha g (F.val.map (homOfLE i).op s) = rho f g i (alpha f s)))
    (Zp : ∀ x : Proj 𝒜, Submodule Rp[x] Np[x])
    (hZp : ∀ x : Proj 𝒜, (Zp x : Set Np[x]) = degreeZeroFractions
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set S)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 n : Set M)) T[x]) :
    ∃ (tau : ∀ x : Proj 𝒜,
      (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (Proj 𝒜).toRingedSpace x).obj F →+ Zp x),
      (∀ (x : Proj 𝒜) (r : (Proj 𝒜).presheaf.stalk x)
        (s : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (Proj 𝒜).toRingedSpace x).obj F),
        tau x (r • s) = (stalkIso 𝒜 x).hom r • tau x s) ∧
      (∀ (x : Proj 𝒜) (f : Fidx) (hx : x ∈ D[f]) (m : ℕ) (y : M)
        (q : Z f) (t : T[x]),
        (q : N[f]) = mk y (⟨f.val.1 ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f.val.1) →
        (t : S) = f.val.1 ^ m →
        (tau x (TopCat.Presheaf.germ F.val.presheaf D[f] x hx
          ((alpha f).symm q)) : Np[x]) = mk y t)
